title: Mindfulness Meditation to Reduce Cognitive Load
official: Mindful Meditation to Reduce Stress and Cognitive Load for Older Adults
summary: Older adults from disadvantaged backgrounds may score lower on memory and thinking tests because of test anxiety and stress, not because of true memory problems. This can lead to being wrongly diagnosed with dementia. This study will test whether a short, 15-minute guided meditation before taking a memory and thinking test helps older adults do better on the test and feel less stressed. About 60 adults age 50 and older, with lower education and income levels, will take part. Participants will be randomly assigned to either listen to a guided meditation or listen to a neutral story for 15 minutes before taking the test. The study will measure stress using heart rate, blood pressure, saliva samples, and a stress questionnaire.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 50 years or older
* Self-identified low educational attainment (high school diploma or less)
* Low socioeconomic status per local criteria
* Able to provide informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

* Diagnosis of dementia
* Uncorrected hearing impairment preventing completion of the audio-guided intervention
* Uncorrected vision impairment preventing completion of the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA)
* Current regular mindfulness meditation practice
* Diagnosis of atrial fibrillation
